main_text.l: tis potentia. Aliud demum nascitur dubiū:
quomodo uidelicet id fiat, ut idem sit agęs
& patiens, quū nihil à se ipso patiatur, sed
semper ab alio quod contrarium sit. Pro-
pterea Aristoteles libro, de Generatione a-
nimalium primo, rectè uidetur negare fe-
men esse materiale principium, ubi ipsum
coagulo comparat. Quibus in generibus
(inquit) mas & fœmina distinguuntur, mas
præbet formam & agens est principium,
fœmina uero corpus atq; materiam: atque
ut in lactis concretione lac ipsum est cor-
pus, coagulum autem densandi cogendiq;
principium obtinet. Qua similitudine fe-
me, quod coagulo comparat, duntaxat esse
agens, & sanguinem maternum, qui uelut
lac est, principium passiuum perspicuè de-
monstrat. At uero Hippocrates & Galenus
longè secus existimant. Semen enim nō so-
lummodo esse principium agens, sed etiā
patiens profitetur: quorū sententia rationi
consentanea est. Nam podagricos, calculo-
sos & epilepticos patres gignere filios his
morbis affines & obnoxios, nullis dubium
est. Atqui huiusmodi affectus præter natu-
ram à generandi facultate non oriuntur,
quia spirituosa duntaxat est, & uitalis calor

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the header; the final digit of 287 is slightly blurred. "dubiū" and "quū" have macrons that are faint on the scan; "nō" and "etiā" likewise. "Quafimilitudine" is printed as one word; given here as "Qua similitudine" with a space, as the sense requires. The bottom-left stain and show-through are not transcribed. The line "feminis," is the catchword, placed under the last line. Printed text is the Latin as copied; no further doubtful readings.
